human-level agents require semantic comprehension and instruction-following
capabilities, which exactly fall into the strengths of LLMs. Although there have
been several initial attempts to build human-level agents based on LLMs, the
theoretical foundation remains a challenging open problem. In this paper, we
propose a novel theoretical cognitive architecture, the Unified Mind Model (UMM),
which offers guidance to facilitate the rapid creation of autonomous agents with
human-level cognitive abilities. Specifically, our UMM starts with the global
workspace theory and further leverage LLMs to enable the agent with various
cognitive abilities, such as multi-modal perception, planning, reasoning, tool use,
learning, memory, reflection and motivation. Building upon UMM, we then develop
an agent-building engine, MindOS, which allows users to quickly create domain-
/task-specific autonomous agents without any programming effort 3.
